:::{#exm-distribution-model}
#### A normal distribution model with a mean function

Let $\modmem$ be a [mean-function model](#def-model-family) (a line, for instance) and $\varpar > 0$ a variance.
The distribution model $\distmem$ that gives each covariate value $\predvar$
the [normal distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-normal)
with mean $\modmemf{\predvar}$ and variance $\varpar$ is

$$
\Outvar \given \Predvar = \predvar
\sim \ndist{\modmemf{\predvar}, \varpar}.
$$ {#eq-normal-distribution-model}

The mean parameter of a normal distribution is its mean,
so @eq-distribution-model-mean-function gives

$$
\meanfnoff{\distmem}{\predvar}
= \modmemf{\predvar}.
$$ {#eq-normal-distribution-model-mean-function}

The mean function $\modmem$ is the component of $\distmem$ that says where the outcome is centered,
and $\varpar$ is the component that says how far it spreads.

:::
